utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Good morning, everybody. All the accused are here except Accused Pandurevic who had given notice that he would be absent today for personal reasons and who has in addition waived his right to be present. From the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Ms. Tapuskovic, and that's it. Prosecution is represented by Mr. McCloskey. The witness is present. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to introduce our intern from our team, Ms. Jana Burasova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, good morning and welcome. So Ms. Nikolic, first of all, let me just make sure that the colonel is okay, is feeling fine. Colonel Vuga, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. What could be done was done and I am well. Thank you very much for your understanding. I have recovered and I'm able to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good. Let's hope you survive the whole sitting. So let's start with Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I will start my examination-in-chief by the rules of the brigade and the special part of your report. When you dealt with the provisions on security and the functions of the security organ in the rules of the brigade, can you please tell us, who is it that the security organ in the brigade is immediately subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ of the brigade command is immediately subordinated to the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the brigade rules, in the Republika Srpska, was it the basis for the commander to control and command the military police and the security organ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the documents that I analysed, the brigade rules were the basis for the control and command over the security organs in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain the significance of the command over the security organ within the framework of a brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The significance of command over the security organ within the framework of a brigade reflects in the fact that the function of security in the brigade is implemented through command within the framework of the regulations, and this is within the purview of the brigade commander, and when it comes to security, the brigade commander has to deal with that through the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your testimony so far, you have explained the terms of commanding a military police company and you said that it is the commander of the unit on which strength the military police company is is in command of that military police company. Is the same true of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is also true of any brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In professional terms, who commands the military company unit?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the brigade, it is the security organ of the brigade, i.e. the chief of the security organ in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on page 3, line 15, in my question, in professional terms, who controls, the word "control" has been erroneously interpreted as "commands."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your testimony so far, Colonel, you have explained the instruction on the command and control of the security and intelligence organ of the Main Staff which was issued on the 26th of October, 1994. At this point, we will not need the document, but I have a question relative to item 2 of this instruction. If you can remember the document that I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you were testifying about item 2, you mentioned the state security as well, in light of the command. Was that a mistake in the interpretation or does the security organ have a certain role in the command of something that concerns state security?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ in the command is stipulated as the professional organ for the affairs of state security, i.e., those affairs that the state security as a whole performs within the civilian bodies, and in the military organs, it is the security organ who performs those duties in keeping with the rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Another question relative to item 2: Could you please just shortly summarise what are the activities in which the security organ has full independence as prescribed by item 2 of the instruction? Would you like me to jog your memory by showing you the document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't need to see the document. It is very clear and it has been said so far but I repeat, a security organ has full independence in applying methods and tools used by the security organ within the framework as prescribed by the rules of service of the security organ, and by the instructions on the method of work of the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Is this the only segment of the activity in which this independence reflects?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the only segment which differs from other activities performed by the security organ and other organs of the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What about Mr. Drago Nikolic? What were his duties within the counter-intelligence jobs as a security organ with regard to the rules of the brigade that were at the time applied in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work of the security organ in the Zvornik Brigade consisted of two different parts or fields. The first field was in the command as a command organ for three groups of jobs and tasks. Those were the staff security tasks, the tasks of controlling military police in professional terms, and jobs arising from the law on criminal procedure in the face of pre-crime -- criminal procedure. The second field was the field of counter-intelligence and Drago Nikolic performed those in keeping with the rules of service and the instruction on the methods and tools of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday, you explained the aspect of security threat in the Drina Corps. Could you please tell us which circumstances had an impact on the security threat in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the framework of the jobs that I've just spoken about, within the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade, there were several security threats which existed throughout the whole period of the implementation of the brigade's tasks. Those were sabotage and terrorist groups that were infiltrated in the area of the brigade's responsibility and that represented a major threat to the brigade. Those were also problems that prevailed within the brigade itself and the only thing I want to say about those is this: In 1994, there were searches launched for 3.369 persons from the brigade and for 821 persons and so on and so forth. In other words, there is information testifying to that kind of threat.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Colonel. We'll come to that document. I would like to follow up on your words so far and show you a document that contains all the information that you have just tackled. Could I please call document 5D265 in e-court? This is under tab 37, if you want to look at that document in hard copy. This is in your binder 1, tab 37. Colonel, this is a document issued by the General Staff of the Army of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was issued in Kladanj on the 28th of May, 1996. It contains a report on the delivery of ammunition and materiel and technical equipment into the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica. Under item 1, you can see the territory where this was done. Was that the zone of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the territory of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain the abbreviation UBS and MTS?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: UBS are lethal combat means, and MTS are materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will no longer need this document. Let me go back to your testimony that you provided yesterday. The pages of the transcript are 23237 and 23278 for my learned friends. You testified about the vetting of volunteers who joined the VRS units, which was a long-term task of the security organ in the corps. In order to avoid showing the same document again, let me ask you this: Did the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade had any tasks to carry out pursuant to this document in April of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What were the obligations of the security organ in the brigade when faced with the problem of the reception of volunteers?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When faced with the issue of the reception of volunteers in the brigade, they had to look at the situation in counter-intelligence terms, in order to establish their true intentions and motives for which they had volunteered to join the VRS. There were ample reasons to act in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I would like to call Exhibit number P2468 in e-court. For you, Colonel, if that is easier for you, in hard copy, binder 1, tab 43. This is a document issued by the General Staff of the VRS on the 20th of April, 1995. Two volunteers trained in the Foreign Legion are sent to the VRS. What were the obligations of the security organ of the brigade in case of the arrival of volunteers from a foreign state? Was that an additional task imposed on the security organs?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've analysed this document. The obligations of the security organ in such cases were very serious and called for their full engagement. There was a lot of ambiguities with regard to foreigners or people of this profile, and the risk of accepting them in any of the units was very high. That's why the security organ, for as long as they were in the unit, it had to have a complete insight into their behaviour and actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was that another task that the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade dealt with in spring 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was one of the tasks of the security organ during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to call Exhibit P5333 [as interpreted] in e-court. You have already testified about this operation yesterday but my question to you is this: When we look at this document -- The number is wrong, 3033 is the right number. Thank you. My question is this: Was this document sent to the chief of security of the Zvornik Brigade who was supposed to deal with this issue and this operative action?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What were the obligations of the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade with regard to this action?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the explanation that was provided yesterday about the operative action, the obligations of the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade were to use their sources of information and to apply various methods of work in order to discover and collect any information and any activity that might point to the indicators that concerned the operative action Judas.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to call document 3D342. It is tab 21 in binder 1 for you, sir. I have to explain that we have not received an official translation for this document. The Defence team has translated just the first page in order to show the origin of the document and I would kindly ask for page 15 in B/C/S and page 2 in English. This is the report of the Zvornik Brigade for the period of 1994. Can we now move to the part concerning the security, security support? Do you have that document in front of you, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it in electronic form.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My question to you is this: Could you please provide comment on this document? Can you tell the Trial Chamber what is it about?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document contains information and data on the briefing about combat security for the period between the 1st of January, 1994, and the 31st of December, 1994. This document deals with the tasks and duties of the security organ, in terms of the security support for that period. There is a list of issues that were relevant for the command and for the engagement of the security organ within the command function. The issues contained in this document were varied, there were all sorts of activities that came to the fore. It is highlighted here that the counter-intelligence work occupied a very important position and it was given a lot of significance. Obviously, in addition to just stating that, we couldn't go any further in this document for obvious reasons. Another issue is leak of information and everything concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the bottom part of the text in the B/C/S, the paragraph which starts with the words, "In the past year."

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found the passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was this the task that Drago Nikolic was occupied with in the course of 1994 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question begs for a brief explanation. When we look at the extent of the engagement of the military police on the tasks related to searches, which partly fell within the remit of counter-intelligence activities, then one can grasp the enormous extent of that job. There were more than 10 searches for different individuals on a daily basis, and these were men who were members of the brigade and of the various units within the AOR of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can we call up document 3D340 in e-court? Colonel, for you, that's tab 20. This is a document of the Zvornik Brigade dated the 18th of March, 1995, and it's in binder 2. The order was signed by the Zvornik Brigade commander. The order has to do with the prevention of desertion and unauthorised abandonment of post on the part of soldiers. Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Would you kindly tell me what sort of activity of the security organ is this and to whom was the security organ responsible for completing this task within the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was answering an earlier question on briefing, this is in fact something that followed that particular briefing, which was the prevention of desertion and unauthorised departure of soldiers from units. The security organ and the military police had a great deal of work in that regard. I've already said what the extent -- the scope of the job and the substance was. The security organ was responsible for these tasks to the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the past couple of days, you've testified a great deal about the activities and duties of the security organs and their cooperation with various associates. I will show you a document that we received two days ago from the OTP. It will be a new document for you. And can we call up 3D444, please? This is a document of the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade dated the 12th of May, 1994, signed by Drago Nikolic. This is a conversation with one of the collaborators. Can we please zoom in as far as possible? The Colonel can -- so the Colonel can see. Thank you. This document reads, "From conversations with collaborator Dragan in addition to the data collected earlier on, we came by the following intelligence." And then the text continues. Colonel, was the identity of a source or a collaborator a secret for the security organ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The identity of a source is definitely a secret for third parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does a security officer have sources within his own unit? Was it possible for the Zvornik Brigade to have sources who were in fact individual members of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ of the Zvornik Brigade had sources primarily among members of their own unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us turn to a different document now, the number is 3D436. For your benefit, Colonel, that's tab 6 of binder 2. This is document dated the 6th of July, 1995. These were instructions of the Main Staff on the work of the military police check-points. The instructions were issued by the Drina Corps command, that's to say its security department, and sent to chiefs of organs for these particular activities, among others those of the Zvornik Brigade. Colonel, can you please comment on this document and tell us what sort of tasks the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade was assigned with after the 6th of July, 1995 as per this document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instructions belonged to the documents which regulated the security regime in the territory of Republika Srpska within the competence of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. The instructions had to do with the work of military police check-points according to a single criterion whereby, for the professional management of the military police, it was the security organs who had that responsibility and the instruction alerts to the fact that the tasks performed by the military police had to be strictly carried out in keeping with the requirements that were issued in earlier instructions and orders, and reaffirmed new requirements that were being put in place with regard to the control of movement of individuals and anything else that came within the purview of a military police check-point, which was quite extensive.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was this one of the documents, one of the instructions, which aimed at providing professional guidance to the security organ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Staff stipulated in the instructions the responsibility of the professional chain -- of the chain of command of the professional organs for the responsibilities held by these professional organs. However, it was the corps commanders and commanders at lower levels who were made responsible for their work, the corps commander and the commanders immediately subordinate to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In July 1995, when you were drafting your report and looking at the documents from that period, did you make any inferences about the activities of the military police and was it engaged in tasks other than strictly military police tasks?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police was engaged in other tasks, not only in military policing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know which tasks were those?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police was engaged in combat as a combat unit that was part of other Zvornik Brigade units.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When the military police was engaged in combat, did this disrupt the work of the 6th of July, 1995, instructions pursuant to which the -- according to which the professional security organ had certain duties to implement and did this disrupt the work of the security organ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any departure from the strictly stipulated activities causes disruption. In this particular instance, the situation was more complex because of the specificity of the nature of activities carried out at the check-points. They sought additional guidance. They also asked for personnel with senior experience because there were problems which could only be solved if there were men experienced enough in solving these problems. This would be the basic explanation of the disruption that it might have caused.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When we are talking about the organisation of the security organs of the Zvornik Brigade, in addition to the security chief, who else was involved in the establishment of the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Zvornik Brigade, as part of the security organ, there was also the desk officer, Milorad Trbic, a captain by rank, who had some duties to carry out which were those of the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In terms of the situations that arose, which you came to realise when you were reviewing the documents, did you see ever Drago Nikolic having to depart from the duties that were strictly security organ duties in the course of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the documents I reviewed, I found information to the effect that Drago Nikolic was assigned to carry out stints of duty as an operations duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: According to the rules of service of the security organ, was the security organ ever to be assigned on duty to the organs -- the internal organs of the brigade or its units?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rule 93 of the rules states quite explicitly that the security organ should not be assigned to perform the duties of operations duty officers for the needs of internal organs of a unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And why is that, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two reasons for that. First, item 48 or Rule 48 of the rules stipulates that the competent commanding officer of a security organ may issue the security organ or the security officer with tasks which fall within his purview and which are not otherwise carried out at the establishment post to which he has been assigned but only within the remit that has been determined. The duty of an operations duty officer and of an internal service of a unit went beyond the purview of the duties of the security organ. That's why the Rule 93 strictly prohibits them from being assigned to those posts because their very responsibilities and duties are being called into question or jeopardised when or if they are assigned to perform such duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just intervene for the transcript? Page 14, line 20, we have the words "competent commanding officer" whereas the witness said, "Senior officer."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The term "staresina" is sometimes interpreted as senior officer, sometimes as commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This -- the term used was the competent senior officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, that's page 23261, lines 3 to 25, you referred to document 3D355. Can we call up the document, please? This is tab 38 of binder 1, for your benefit, should you need the document. I'll put the question to you, since we've already discussed it. I hope you'll be able to answer without consulting it again. There, it was said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can Madam Nikolic please read slowly when reading? It is impossible to interpret at this pace.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You described there that the forces of the BH Army, by setting up false radio networks and shelling Zvornik created the situation where there was a possibility of the town being attacked on the 13th of July, 1995. My question is: What was the role of the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade in such a situation as soon as they came to know that the town could possibly be attacked on the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the tasks of the counter-intelligence work of the security organ is to detect any and all indications of, as the rules state, possible aggression, whereas for the Zvornik Brigade, that meant the indications of a possible attack. The indications fell within the usual assessment of the counter-intelligence service on the basis of which Drago Nikolic had to take urgent counter-intelligence measures, in accordance with the brigade rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your yesterday's testimony, you commented upon a number of documents with colleague Zivanovic, 1D698 for instance, 3D317 and so on and so forth. It had to do with the order on mobilisation at the corps level but it had to do with the Zvornik Brigade. Do you need to look at the document? Or can I proceed with putting my question to you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can put the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As the chief of the security organ of the brigade, did Drago Nikolic have the duty to apply brigade rules? This was in mid-July, I believe it was the 15th of July, when mobilisation had to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 15th of July at 9.25 in Zvornik to be precise. The document of the Drina Corps concerning mobilisation were issued -- was issued later. What I meant to say by this is the following: The first body or individual who should have acted upon that mobilisation order was in Drago Nikolic's hands. That was the first move that was taken by him in relation to the defence of Zvornik. The situation dictated for him to do everything in his power in order for the defence to be organised smoothly, in particular, from the point of view of security and specifically within the field of activity of Drago Nikolic. There were specific obligations determined in the rules of mobilisation and we commented upon them already.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Before we look at another document issued by the Zvornik Brigade in July 1995, I would like to ask something. Is it customary that brigades issue their monthly plans of work which describe amongst other things the work of the security organ and its tasks?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an obligation upon all the commands. They have to have their plans of work that will govern them in the work and in the performance of their tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could I now call for 3D443 to be put in e-court? For your benefit, sir, this is tab 9, binder 2, page 7 in B/C/S, page 11 in English. This is the plan of work of the Zvornik Brigade for the month of July 1995. Do you have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Under bullet point 70 in chapter 6, the title is, "Security organ or the organ for OB tasks." And then look at 77, this is where the tasks performed by Drago Nikolic in the course of July 1995 are described. Would you please be so kind and tell us what were the tasks that were carried out by the security organ according to this plan in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you just briefly because these are groups of tasks. Bullet point 70, security vetting of persons. 71, briefing in battalions and divisions. 72, security -- briefing of security organs when it comes to security and intelligence. 73, work pursuant to the request of the sectors of the security intelligence of the Main Staff, the department of security and intelligence of the Drina Corps and other organs of other units for security intelligence. The security processing of persons in the territory and some details are provided. Work on the planning, organisation and performance of military and professional training of the military police company. And meeting with the military police company. Those are the tasks of the security organ of the command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You have studied the entire document and we will not look at it page by page. My question to you is this: The plan of the work of the Zvornik Brigade for July 1995, does it envisage a task pointing to the fact that Krivaja 95 operation was being prepared, that the tactical group would be formed and sent out of the area of the brigade and that prisoners of war would arrive at the territory of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no such tasks in this plan. There is not even a hint of any such possibility in this plan of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go back for a moment to document P106. If you remember, this is the preparatory order of the Drina Corps dated the 2nd of July, 1995. And also document P107, another order issued by the Drina Corps, this time for the active combat, dated 2nd July, 1995. Do you need the documents, Colonel, before I put a couple of questions to you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can put your questions without the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Based on these orders, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, in July 1995, did he issue his own orders basing his orders on the order of the Drina Corps for active combat?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did issue his own order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can we now please look at document P318 in e-court? Tab 41, binder 1, for your benefit, sir. Is this the order, Colonel, if you have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document, and this is the order issued by the commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The date is 2nd of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. I have omitted that from my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You've read this document, haven't you? And my question is this: Does this document contain a part referring to security, prisoners of war, war booty, which was something that the order of the Drina Corps for active combat dated 12 July 1995 points to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not contained, there is no such information, there are no such tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you explain why?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit that was established from the strength of the Zvornik Brigade performed its tasks out of the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade, outside of the area of defence of the Zvornik Brigade. And by virtue of that fact, all the issues that you just mentioned were dealt with outside of the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade and outside of the scope of authority of its security organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When Tactical Group 1 left for Srebrenica which is something this document points to, did something change in the security and the tasks relative to the intelligence and security in the Zvornik Brigade at the beginning of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When a unit of such composition and strength left the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade, this required from the security organ to carry out a new intelligence and security assessment because the situation had changed to a great extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is the change reflected in?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is reflected in two important issues. The first is the departure of some of the troops that had performed tasks in the units, some of which concerned the security regime that they controlled, and the second would be the departure of some of the sources who provided information to the security organ, some of them were collaborators of the security organs. This left a gap in the area of responsibility of the brigade in the part that they covered, and this had to be dealt in the forthcoming period with reassigning the tasks of the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you provided comment on document P3025. We can call it up in e-court, if you wish. This is an order of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade which was issued pursuant to the order of the corps for active combat, P107. This order features item 10, concerning security, war booty and prisoners of war, whereas in the order of the Zvornik Brigade, this particular segment is lacking. Could you please tell us why, why the orders of the subordinated commands were such as they were?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order of the commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade dated 5 July 1995, and the order issued by the commander of the Tactical Group 1, which was separated from the Zvornik Brigade, differ because the Bratunac Brigade carried out combat activities in its own area of responsibility and the issues concerning prisoners of war are within the remit of the commander of the Bratunac Infantry Brigade. On the other hand, leaving the area of responsibility for a territory outside of the area of responsibility implies that these issues will be dealt with in the territory where combat is taking place. This is the first difference. And the second difference is contained in the very order issued by the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. He deals with the issues in the way stipulated herein, and if you need my comment, I will gladly provide it as need be.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the 2nd and 3rd of July, 1995. What happened with the rest of the Zvornik Brigade and the chief of security of the Zvornik Brigade at the beginning of July 1995? Did he follow the tactical group? Is he involved in Krivaja 1995 or did he have other tasks and duties that he was involved in?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ of the command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade remained in his area of responsibility, and worked according to the plan that we have just seen, that had been issued by the command, and he dealt with the problems that have been discussed and that would arise within the ensuing period, in other words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object. This is testifying as if he is a fact witness on the ground. If he is testifying as to what he sees in documents or what he has read as we have seen him thus far, I have no objection, but there was no proceeding about that. He is now testifying as if he is a fact witness on the ground telling us what Drago Nikolic is doing. I think there needs to be a connection to something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand you perfectly well. I think Mr. McCloskey is right. Perhaps you can ask the colonel on what is he basing the statements that he's just made in trying to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will follow your guideline.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Colonel, the description that you provided and the answers to my questions, what are they based on?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm basing my answers on the analysis of the documents that was provided to me and placed at my disposal containing, first of all, the plan of work; second of all, the order of the commander of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade in which Drago Nikolic did not leave the territory of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. Thirdly, I'm basing my answers on the fact that there is no single document testifying to the fact that Drago Nikolic might have left the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade in that time. If that had been the case, this should have been documented. These are the facts that I'm basing my conclusions on. And they are the result of my analysis of the documents that were made available to me while I was writing my report. Everything is based on that and I don't have any other information testifying to the fact that Drago Nikolic was not in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. The plan speaks about his work and what he did at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Given the situation that prevailed in Zvornik at the time, I would kindly ask the witness to be shown another document which is P311. For you, sir, this is tab 10. This is the record of the presence of the Zvornik Brigade for the month of July 1995. Tab 10, binder 2, for you, sir. Can we go to page 3 in B/C/S and page 2 in English in e-court? Under 38, on page -- that you have before you, you can see the name of Drago Nikolic. Can you see it actually?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If we look at the 12th of July, could you please tell us what is indicated there and what are -- is the meaning of the indications and markings in these columns next to each of the names?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Plus" denotes presence. "S" denotes off duty. And "T" denotes field duty, which means that the person was on a field duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If you look at the 12th of July, you will see the markings "S." Would it be unusual for the chief of security to be off duty on the 12th of July, and for him not to be present in the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no reason for this to be unusual, if that's how the work on that day had been organised, and if the situation provided for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: According to the documents you studied, which events had any impact on the security situation in the Zvornik Brigade after the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documents I had at my disposal, I concluded, based on several important situations which took place during the time you're asking me about, the first one was the one we've discussed, which continued, and that was the departure of the unit and the process that the Tactical Group 1 was included in. The process of counter-intelligence work had to develop in the direction that we have already discussed. Therefore, I won't go into it again. The breakthrough of the column from Srebrenica into the area of the Zvornik Brigade was a new security-related event which created a new security situation, in which Drago Nikolic had his tasks as the security organ. The threat of an attack on Zvornik was an additional security threat, and Drago Nikolic had his tasks pertaining to that as well. There are also other regular tasks that Drago Nikolic was supposed to carry out in keeping with the newly arisen situation and together with the new tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Briefly said, based on everything you've said so far, what was the degree of threat for the security of the command and facilities in the territory of Zvornik on the 13th and 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the size and type of threat that could be ascertained, one can talk about the presence of a total threat. In the document on mobilisation and the request for commanders Pandurevic and Jolovic's return there was a warning concerning a possible disaster.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I please ask for a break at this moment before I move on to another topic? And I believe my examination will be shorter than I announced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have a 25-minute break starting now. Thank you. --- Break taken at 10.13 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I would like to go back to the issue of POWs. In the past few days during your testimony you mentioned the general mobilisation within the framework of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Could we please have Exhibit 3D313 in e-court? It is your tab 47, page 2 in B/C/S and page 2 in English? We have the document in front of us. Have you found it, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th of June, 1992, a general mobilisation was declared in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That meant that all military conscripts were to report to their units under the conditions described. We have discussed that so far. At the same time, in practice, as illustrated by the example of Srebrenica, it meant that all military-aged men, all conscripts, who were being escorted by an armed part of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were, to all intents and purposes, mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, that meant that they became members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once mobilised, they were deployed into various units, under the control of the commands which had mobilised them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could we next in e-court have document P196? I would now move on to the topic of POWs. It is your tab 7 -- 70, binder 1. It is a document by the security organ of the Drina Corps, the date is the 15th of April, 1995. The title is, "Escort of POWs." Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Based on this document, who were those who were supposed to implement this task that was issued by the Drina Corps to the security organ? Who are those responsible?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two significant issues at hand. The first one is what was the level that was responsible for the POWs. What they also need to bear in mind was where these POWs were to be collected, held, and how were they supposed to be treated as of the point of collection to or through the process of escorting them to a higher command. That was the scope of the work to be done. Professional security criteria was provided, under which those locations were to be chosen and what criteria had to be met. Those are the two issues. Along the professional line of control, the security organs were supposed to deal with the situation up to the level of battalion because the battalions had security intelligence clerks, desk officers, who were supposed to deal with these professional issues in the battalions to which they had been assigned and in which they could have an insight into how the task was being carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We will no longer need this document. Based on the documents you studied when drafting your report, and exhibits, you are familiar with the fact that at a certain moment a group of POWs was brought to the area of Zvornik in July 1995. They were accommodated in various schools in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. My question is this: Did the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade, based on the rules of the security organs have the right and duty to visit the facilities where the POWs were housed. According to certain testimonies, Drago Nikolic was seen in front of two schools in Petkovci, in Orahovac, where the POWs were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wanted to conclude my question first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your question? It still looks leading to me, from what we have from lines 22 on the previous page until line 6, page 27, but what is your question could help us decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The answer is in the question, that's my problem, on a sensitive spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't know what the question is so let's wait to see what the question is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to narrow it down to a single question but I can go with open questions one by one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Colonel, when drafting your report and studying the documents, did you learn that certain POWs were brought in the area of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documents I had at my disposal, there is information that the POWs were brought in the environs of Zvornik, that is the area of the Zvornik Brigade. There are several sources confirming that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you conclude from the sources what the facilities used to accommodate the POWs were?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were public facilities: Schools and the cultural hall or the community hall in one or two cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether these facilities were in the settlements or outside of the settlements?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given their original purpose, such facilities were usually in the centres of settlements, to be equally accessible to all of the residents to the extent possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If there was a number of POWs in the territory of a unit encompassed by the Zvornik Brigade and its security organ, does the security organ have an obligation to gain an insight into the situation?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Accommodating a number of POWs in the situation -- in the security situation as it was in the area of the Zvornik Brigade, represented a new security fact that the security organ had to bear in mind when performing his tasks, since that could have posed a potential threat for the command and the units of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Based on the organisational composition of the security organ of the brigade, based on the rules of the brigade and the rules of the security organs, was Drago Nikolic as the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade capable of doing anything to prevent the POWs being accommodated in the various schools?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having in mind everything you've mentioned and having in mind the rules governing the work of security organs, the security organ had no impact on the decision whether the POWs would be distributed across the area of responsibility of the brigade and concerning which facilities will be used.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you come across a single document which would point to the contrary?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the operational combat documents I used to arrive at my conclusions, there was no information which would testify to the contrary of what I've just said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could we please show the colonel document 3D352 next? It is a Zvornik Brigade document of the 25th of August, 1995 -- excuse me, the 24th of August. It is your tab 24 in binder 2. Do you have the document, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you study this document when drafting your report? If you did, could you please tell us what it entails?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did study it, from the point of view of security, it was not of any particular interest for me when making my conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If we look at line 4 of the document, it says, "The exchange was supposed to take place in the region of the village and chief security was appointed on behalf of the command for the control of the above-mentioned activity." What was the activity concerned and why was the chief of security appointed for that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a humanitarian issue of family reunification. That part of work by its nature does not fall under the remit of the security organ. However, if there was an estimate that there were some security-related issues involved in that, a commander could have ordered the chief of security to be represented, to take part in the task.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We will not be needing the document any longer. Thank you. Can we now have another document, which is P3425? For you, Colonel, that's tab 8 of binder 2, the one you have before you now. This is a piece of intelligence, admittedly from 1993, signed by Drago Nikolic. Colonel, please read the document through and if you're familiar with it, please tell us what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of the drafting of the document, the Zvornik Infantry Brigade had, as part of its -- the same establishment, the security intelligence structure performing two sets of activities, namely, security-related activities and intelligence-gathering activities. This particular document relates to the intelligence branch and that's why it's titled, "Intelligence," in fact. At the time, this fell within the competence of the structure, the chief of which was Drago Nikolic. The document points to the activities aimed at gathering intelligence and developing measures to counter the activities involved. I won't go through the document itself. I think it's quite self-evident.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Colonel, does this have to do with the use of communications in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has primarily to do with the use of communications, because the intelligence gathering was primarily focused on the means of communications and information that could be gathered through those means.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Based on the documentation you studied, do you know when it was that the security organ and the intelligence organ split to form two separate, independent structures or organs?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organs of the VRS, or the security and intelligence organs of the VRS, were separated pursuant to an order dated the 13th of January, 1995, and these organs were separated down the chain of command. The intelligence organ became part of the staff of the headquarters, and the security organ was a separate structure that was immediately subordinated to the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we call up document 3D319 in e-court? That's tab 78 of binder 1. This is a document of the Drina Corps dated the 23rd of June, 1995. Do you have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the document is about, who sent the document, and to whom?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the Drina Corps command, specifically from the department for intelligence and security tasks, dated the 23rd of May, 1995. I conclude that it's -- the number there is 5, that's to say May, but it may be 6, I'm not sure, but definitely the day is the 23rd, and the year 1995. It was sent to the chiefs of intelligence and security of subordinate units, and I'll not go into them but among them is the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. The document relates to the discipline in radio communication, and the top headline is, "Observation." By its nature, the document is similar to the one we've looked at a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: To what extent were the subordinate organs duty-bound to act upon a document titled, "Observation"?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document providing guidance, and any organ is duty-bound to conduct a security assessment in one's own unit pursuant to this particular observation, and to take measures that fall within one's purview and propose them to the commander, in keeping with the rules governing confidentiality and secrecy of documents and communications.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on the documents we've just looked at, and specifically this one concerning observations about radio communications, can you tell us, as an officer who has a specialty in communications, would a chief act in contravention of such observations and orders and disclose information that was secret, that's to say that 1.000 POWs would be sent into the area from the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Colonel. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That is calling for speculation. If he wants to say according to the rules, but for him to go into whether he would or would not as an expert witness is complete speculation and not -- does not call for his expertise, whether someone would break the rules. How does he know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, do you wish to comment on that, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One point, Your Honours. I will rephrase the question. However, in view of all the documents and the witness's experience, I believe that the colonel would be able to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see how the rephrased question looks like. Then we check with the colonel to what extent he can answer the question without speculating.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Colonel, would a security officer act in breach of his own instructions and observations received from the superior command?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I can say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's exactly my point. Anybody can do anything, and his expert opinion -- he could say what the results might be of someone not following their own orders but this is just pure speculation. Do people do things that are wrong? Do people do things that are inconsistent? This is what the Court is here to decide. We don't need him to tell us that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Let me consult with my colleagues, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We agree with the position taken by Mr. McCloskey, so please move to your next question. We feel we are -- we don't need the witness to tell us what you are seeking to get from him, Ms. Nikolic. So let's proceed with your next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one -- I do not -- just to clarify I do not have an objection to this witness saying why it would be stupid or counter-productive or something to not follow one's own orders. That I don't have a problem with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also think that we don't need the -- I think it stands to reason. It doesn't need an expert to draw some conclusions. Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In view of my learned friend's position, I will put this one question to you: How important is it to follow one's own orders and instructions governing communication?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, own orders are drafted on the basis of the knowledge of the issues for the purpose of which the order is issued, and with a view to resolving problems out in the field. Secondly, in drafting one's own orders, the person involved must be well-informed about the issue at hand in order to be able to inform others. This was important in every branch of military activity but particularly so in the field of security. One needs to be well-informed on matters concerning which one provides assessments and further guidance. That would be my answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was part of the responsibility and obligation on the part of Drago Nikolic the issue of ensuring security and safe communication?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The job description of Drago Nikolic stated that he had to prevent leaks of secret military data. All the possible leaks of such information fall within the competence of Drago Nikolic to prevent those, as far as his security position and the command he worked at allowed him to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this in a way a critical moment in the month of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As can be seen, this issue was important throughout the period. However, there were situations which required special attention to be paid to that particular issue, and when the requirement for confidential military intelligence not to be leaked was particularly pronounced.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Nikolic please speak into her microphone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, if you could speak into your microphone, because the interpreters are complaining.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise to the interpreters once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you testified, and this was at pages 23250, 23251 of the transcript, in answer to my learned friend Zivanovic's questions, about a document which I'd like to be shown again, and that's P131. This is a document from General Tolimir dated the 13th of July, 1995. Do you have the document, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the document, Madam Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let's read the last sentence. "It will be best if this were a new group," and they are referring to prisoners, "which has not been in contact with the other prisoners of war." Can you tell us, in the context of the document as a whole, and from a security perspective, what this particular sentence means?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This comes from the part of the instruction issued by the ministry, namely, item 14 of that instruction, which stipulated that POWs can be talked to in order to obtain intelligence useful for the purposes of the VRS. General Tolimir is directing everyone's attention to that point and states that it would be best, from that particular point of view, to regard that group as possibly a new source of information which could be arrived at by the security and intelligence organs, because if they had already been in touch with the POWs, from whom they could have learned what the security organs already came by, in terms of intelligence, this would be a way of painting the whole picture and of double-checking whether all the information gathered from the POWs was accurate. The underlying purpose was to arrive at new intelligence rather than arrive at intelligence that had already been gathered.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I would like to go back to a few issues and a few questions that I would like to ask you about the military police. Could you please tell us who commands a military police company?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A military police company is commanded by the commander of the military police company, and all the principles of command apply to his command as they do in all the other units of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And who is the immediate commander of the commander of the military police company?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the military police company in a brigade is subordinated to the brigade commander, directly or via the security organs, and this is something that will be decided upon by the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Colonel, why is it important for the brigade commander to be in command of the security organ of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is important because the function of the security organ is intended for the protection of the brigade, and the brigade commander is responsible for the brigade, save for its -- for the part that refer to the methods of work of the security organ. And this is something that we have already discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Is there a principle of command in the JNA which is generally known and this is exactly how it is entitled in the military terminology?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two key principles that need to be discussed. One is the unity, singleness of command, and subordination.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My question to you is this: Can the security organ use the military police unit in accordance with the gravity of the task? In other words, he can use the military police unit for minor tasks without consulting either the commander or the person standing in for the commander at any given moment?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the function of command, there are no minor or major tasks. The command function implies the assignment of tasks, their execution and control. There are no minor or major tasks, therefore. With this regard, the security organise did not have the right to use military police for any task without seeking prior approval by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is the nature of relationship between the security organ and the military police with regard to POWs?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The overall nature of relationship between the security organ and the military police is purely professional. The security organ is in relation to prisoners of war when this task is given to the military police, and the role of the security organ and its task was as a professional organ for the control of the military police, which means this: The military police is provided with professional guidance from the point of view of its purview, its tasks, and the information gathered with that regard and tell them how to carry out the tasks in a more efficient way and those tasks are the ones for which the military police is trained to perform them in a military professional sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to put a question to the witness that stems from the testimony of a protected witness. Therefore, I would kindly ask the Court to move into private session to avoid revealing the identity of that protected witness by accident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means. Let's go into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He dealt with the subject matter quite extensively when he was being examined by Mr. Zivanovic, so if you can avoid -- if you have of course new questions and areas on the same subject matter that you would like to explore, please, by all means go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Colonel, according to the instruction on the application of the rules of service, what is the role of the MP commander with regard to the function in the brigade, if there is anything that differs with the role from the corps?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A company commander commands the military police unit. It is responsible for its overall condition, combat readiness and the performance of its tasks and either to his superior directly or through the security organ, he proposes the use of the military police unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to call up Exhibit 3D435 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This is tab 28, binder 2. This is the plan of the security measures of the command of the Zvornik Brigade, and its title is, "Stit 95." Did you ever see this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have analysed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This plan contains measures and activities segregated into three segments, in the brigade command, in the units, and in the territory of the brigade, i.e., in the zone of responsibility, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to look at the measures and activities under A, pages 2 and 3 in B/C/S, as well as in English. There are columns with titles, measures and activities, person responsible, time lines, deadlines and so on and so forth. According to this document, could you tell us, when it comes to the measures of the brigade command, which measures and activities is independently controlled by the chief of security in cooperation with the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are measures and activities under items 6 and 7 of the plan. Furthermore, items 8 and 9, where the chief of OB defines his own tasks. These are the security organs and the others pertain to the chief of the security organ. I've already spoken about the difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. We have a mistake in the transcript. Page 40, line 7, [In English] In cooperation with the commander. [Interpretation] He said in cooperation with the superior security organ.

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issue of coordination -- of cooperation with the superior security organ has to be corrected. The guidance is provided by the guidelines of the cooperation with superior organs of security. Cooperation is -- develops with neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Sir, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document represents the foundation for the engagement of the security organ of the command of the Zvornik Brigade and the chief of the security organ of the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Judging by the title page, it is in effect in 1995, or it was in effect in 1995, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document refers to the security measures so-called Stit 95. The specific activities of the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can we now go to page 4 of the same document? Bullet points from 5 through 7, I believe. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. My mistake. Can we please see page 6?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Colonel, could you please explain for us, looking at page 6, what is this document about?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 6 defines and determines the activities, i.e., the obligations, that stem from the territory of certain participants in providing the security regime that is prescribed for that territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can we please go back to page 5, measures and activities in the units. Under bullet point 12, Colonel, can you explain the meaning of bullet point 12?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bullet point 12 describes the situation when the military police performs the tasks -- the task of escorting and securing prisoners of war. The security organ is involved with professional cooperation. That's how it was defined because there was no other column, but the meaning and the sense of the professional role of the security organ is defined in no uncertain terms and it is quite obvious who is the one who commands and controls is the commander and the military police is the executor when this is specially provided for by a special order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind -- and we will no longer need this document, I thank you. Bearing in mind the importance of the security tasks, as you've described them in your testimony, would it be expected from the brigade commander to consult his security organ upon his return from Zepa in order to prepare himself for the major threat that the Zvornik Brigade was facing?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the security organ is subordinated to the commander and the commander could, at any point in time, request from him to submit his security assessment and to propose measures that would bear upon the command and to issue him with a task within his authorities in the area of security.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. This has brought my examination-in-chief to an end. Colonel, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nikolic. It seems like you're going to have an extra day, Mr. Ostojic. You are going next?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: By your leave, the colleagues from the Defence team for Mr. Gvero kindly asked us that they proceed before us and we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I was coming actually to you first, but I understood that to be the case when I saw Mr. Krgovic standing. Yes, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Krgovic and on behalf of the Defence for General Gvero I will put several questions to you in relation to your testimony here so far. I will do my best to formulate my questions so that your answer can be as short as possible, this to save you from having to spend too much time testifying here, and to save time, of course. The interpreters alerted me to the fact that I need to come closer to the microphone. Colonel, in your testimony so far, you referred to numerous rules and regulations of the Yugoslav People's Army, which were used in the VRS. I will show you one of the documents now, namely, 6D305. Can I have the usher's assistance? I have a hard copy for you. This is a methodical manual for military and police training. Can you turn to page 121 of the B/C/S and 209 -- or, rather, that's page 2 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I kindly ask my colleague to provide me with a list of documents he's going to use? Because I've received nothing of the kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Has the Prosecution received a list? Yes. Are you discriminating against the Miletic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that a list was sent to the case managers of all teams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but usually Madam Fauveau is pretty much correct in her statements. So do we have a copy that we could hand to her straight away without --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're going to get one. Thank you. Let's proceed, please. Have you got it, Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not yet, but we may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, the document indicates that when transporting POWs, one has to take extra care to separate officers and common soldiers who had not been interrogated from the ones who have, and to have them transported in segregated groups, is that something that you were able to glean from the document?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you another document, 6D304. [In English] Mr. Usher, please. [Interpretation] This is the methodology of the combat training of the military police. Please, I direct to you page 176, and page 2 -- or rather, sorry, 346, that's page 2 of the English translation. These were the regulations used also by the VRS in the period of time you testified to, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now look at document P131, please.

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It will appear on your screen. That's the document providing information from General Tolimir. My colleague, Jelena Nikolic, read out the last sentence of the document to you. The rules that I've shown you, do they fit into that last sentence? Is that the meaning of that sentence?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated the reasons earlier, and they are in fact contained in the document, which means that they are consistent, both from the point of view of the rules and of the action taken by General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The latter part which refers to the use of the POWs for farming, do you know was there in force a regulation in the Republika Srpska at the time which stipulated that the POWs may be used for certain farm work or farm work in general?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were the instructions for the treatment of POW, of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, and item 10 specifically speaks of their use of the POWs for farm work. Now, the international conventions governing the treatment of POWs also provide for the possibility to use them for farm work unless this is related with any combat activities of the detaining party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you see anything in that document that would be contrary to the rules and regulations in force in the territory of Republika Srpska at the time the document was made?

utterances.speaker: PETAR VUGA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there is nothing in this document that is contrary to the regulations that should have been adhered to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Colonel and Mr. Krgovic, please don't overlap. That's number 1. And secondly, both you, please, if you could slow down a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]
